items.summary: 58 entries re-checked on 28 Sep 2026: 58 unchanged, 0 with new commits, all main links responding; 40 videos re-checked: all available. 0 link problems; 2 dead repositories (fly-survivors, ommatid) excluded. The re-check came about 22 hours after the first pass.

15 new catalogue entries graded from code: 5 A (doom-fly-control, doomfly-rl, Fly Self Driving, flydoom by mutkuoz, a null-model study), 1 B (Fly.exe), 5 C (FlyBridge, fly-api, fly-brain by erojas, Haltere, Kick the Fly), 2 D (FlyBrain-HalfLife, FlyBrain Robot Bridge) and 2 data tools (FlyWire annotations, Virtual Fly Brain).

Is it real?: a third-party control study found that a brainless constant autopilot survives in Doom about as long as DOOMFLY's full-brain simulation (51.9 s vs 53.3 s; shuffled wiring 6.7 s). DOOMFLY stays grade B. New verdict rows for the Half-Life video (grade D: its code builds a synthetic network by default) and the Minecraft farming video (FlyBridge, grade C).
4 new videos in the gallery: the Half-Life video (grade D) and video files from doom-fly-control (A), Fly.exe (B) and flydoom (A).
SWOT's Minecraft farming video now links to its catalogue entry, FlyBridge (grade C).
Text correction: the DOOMFLY limitations text no longer contains internal notes on how its grade was reached; the grade (B) and its reasons are unchanged.
New project pages: DOOMFLY (mechanism, controls, untested run steps) and the Shiu et al. whole-brain model (tested and untested requirements, results, known issues, 17 projects built on it).
Research report of the second check: method, tracking results, new entries, the Doom control study and limits.

New Video gallery: 40 fruit fly brain videos (Doom, Minecraft, Beat Saber, Eon and the lab films), each with its project's evidence grade from the catalogue and what the video does not show. Videos open on their original platform.
First release: 58 fruit fly brain simulation projects, datasets and tools, each with an evidence grade from code, true update dates, licence and link check (28 Sep 2026).

Build your own: a tested beginner guide that runs the fruit fly whole-brain model from an empty folder on 2 CPUs, with exact commands, expected output, a shuffled-wiring control, tests and the full source.
Verdicts on 12 viral fly-brain claims and 13 controlled or negative studies, plus what "91%" and "95%" really mean.
Seven fly connectome datasets compared with data licences (FlyWire is CC BY-NC 4.0) and a reconciliation of the quoted neuron counts.
28 no-install ways to try a fly brain, grouped by what you can do, with honest check labels.
Machine-readable catalogue (projects.json and its JSON Schema) and instructions for AI agents.
First research report: methods, findings, open conflicts and next runs.
